summary:
The SECURE Grid Act amends section 366 of the Energy Policy and Conservation Act, 42 U.S.C. 6326, governing State energy security plans, to require those plans and related State planning processes to address physical security, cybersecurity, resilience, and supply-chain risks affecting local electric distribution infrastructure and equipment for electricity generation, transmission, and distribution.

Section 2 adds to 42 U.S.C. 6326(a) a definition of “local distribution system” as energy infrastructure owned and operated by an electric utility at a voltage of 100 kilovolts or less. It amends section 366(b)(2) to include “suppliers of equipment for the generation, transmission, and distribution of electricity” among the entities relevant to State plan coordination. It revises section 366(c)(3) to require State energy security plans to address potential hazards to each energy sector or system, including physical threats and vulnerabilities—specifically weather-related threats and vulnerabilities, physical attacks on local distribution systems and the bulk-power system, and supply-chain risks for electricity generation, transmission, and distribution equipment—and cybersecurity threats and vulnerabilities, including threats to and vulnerabilities of local distribution systems that may impact the bulk-power system. It revises section 366(c)(5) to require a risk mitigation approach to enhance reliability and end-use resilience, including methods for responding to, mitigating, and recovering from the hazards described in section 366(c)(3).

Section 2 also amends section 366(d)(3) to add entities supplying electricity generation, transmission, and distribution equipment to the categories addressed in State coordination requirements. It restructures section 366(e) and provides that a State submission required for eligibility is not subject to approval by the Secretary of Energy. It amends section 366(f) by changing the Secretary’s authority to provide assistance from discretionary to mandatory. It amends section 366(h) to include “local distribution system” information within the protected-information provision. It replaces section 366(i) with a sunset providing that section 366 expires on September 30, 2031.

Section 3 requires the Comptroller General, not later than September 30, 2030, to submit to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce and the Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources a public report evaluating the efficacy of State energy security plans, Federal financial assistance under part D of title III of EPCA, State activities funded by that assistance, implementation of section 366 as amended, and State use of assistance under section 366(f), with recommendations for State and Department of Energy coordination improvements. Information protected under section 366(h) must be placed in a nonpublic annex.
